newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends lower after LME stock hike.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends lower after LME stock hike.

text.p: COMEX copper settled down but above session lows as the market digested news of another hike in LME stocks.

Copper inventory on the London exchange rose 4,725 tonnes to 143,225 tonnes Tuesday, with 2,625 tonnes of the hike in the U.S., metal taken from COMEX warehouses as a result of arbitrage deals, traders said.
"The market came under downside pressure from the rise in LME stocks and some profit-taking after Monday's upside move," Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities said.
Shortcovering near the lows pared some of the day's losses, she added.
March COMEX settled down 1.30 cents at 106.25 cents a lb, traded 107.95 to 104.80 cents. Spot January slipped 0.55 cent to 109.80 cents.
Volume was estimated at 8,000 lots against Monday's official tally of 8,129 lots.
The LME cash to three months premium or backwardation held firm at $235/$239, lending support to nearby prices.
Raptopoulos said the U.S. copper market was also awaiting with some concern December's housing starts figures, due Wednesday at 0830 EST.
Analysts forecast December starts of 1.47 million on an annual basis, down from the actual rate of 1.514 million in November.

Evidence of growing copper production was seen in the latest figures from Chile's Escondida mine, now the world's largest. The mine produced 841,361 tonnes of copper last year, up from 466,913 tonnes in 1995.
